verdict.summary: Issue #223 is blocked by an unresolved owner-only semantic decision, missing required control-plane labeling, and contradictory/undefined launch-timeout behavior. Ownership, trust boundaries, accounting, validation coverage, dependencies, rollout, and recovery are otherwise substantially specified.

blockingFindings.title: Kill semantics remain an unresolved owner-only decision
blockingFindings.details: The preserved owner goal requires stalled work to be killed, but the specification leaves physical runtime cancellation versus irrevocable logical revocation undecided and explicitly makes that choice a prerequisite for implementation acceptance and activation. No authenticated owner selection is present in the complete issue version. Required action: obtain an authenticated repository-owner answer for issue #223 choosing A (physical cancellation, with an accepted canonical cancellation dependency) or B (logical revocation, explicitly narrowing the meaning of kill).

blockingFindings.title: Current labels do not reflect the specification's blocked owner-decision state
blockingFindings.details: The issue contract requires issue #223 to remain labeled df:ask-owner until the kill-semantics decision is authenticated, but verified current state lists only P1. This makes the durable GitHub control plane disagree with the issue's own required status and can allow sequencing or automation to miss the owner gate. Required action: apply df:ask-owner through the trusted runtime while the decision remains unresolved; df:reviewed must not indicate readiness while blocking findings remain.

blockingFindings.title: Launch-expiry transitions have conflicting outcomes and omit later-invocation deadline initialization
blockingFindings.details: For an admitted invocation lacking canonical binding at expiry, the ambiguous-launch recovery contract requires launch_state_ambiguous followed by outcome launch_ambiguous. The watchdog contract separately defines any expired launch phase as a stall and requires stall_detected followed by outcome stalled, so identical initial-launch state permits two terminal paths. In addition, launch expiry is initialized only at delegation admission and changed to progress after the first binding, while subsequent model turns and retries also use launcher_invocation_admitted and ambiguous-launch recovery without defining an invocation-specific launch phase, expiry, or transition back from progress. Required action: define one authoritative per-invocation launch-deadline transition and deterministic precedence, including later turns and retries, and state whether expiry without binding produces launch_ambiguous or stalled.

nonBlockingNotes: Exact owner question: For issue #223 and epic #218, does “kill stalled work” require A — physical runtime cancellation with authoritative terminal evidence, or B — irrevocable logical revocation with no claim of provider-process termination?
Issues #221 and #222 remain open; the specification correctly treats their accepted and merged interfaces as activation prerequisites and blocks closed if those interfaces are absent.
Issue #255 becomes a blocking dependency only if the owner selects physical cancellation; issue #258 remains a disjoint lifecycle owner.
